name: The O'Leary barn
address: Behind 137 DeKoven Street, on the alley

status.today: The Chicago Fire Academy stands on the site
status.note: The barn burned that night; the site's later history is not researched here.

built.note: Standing in October 1871 (Andreas, volume two). Nobody recorded when it was built; 1864 stands in for the years before the fire.

use: Barn for cows and a horse
summary: A small wooden barn where the O'Learys kept five cows. The Great Chicago Fire began here on Sunday night. Legend says a cow kicked over a lamp, but the inquiry could not prove how it started.

key.label: Animals
key.value: Five cows, a calf and a horse

notable.text: High wooden fences ran from the barn to the sheds next door, and carried the fire to them.
Dennis Sullivan saw the fire from across the street and ran in to save the animals.
No picture of the barn is known: this one is built from the inquiry's description.

story.text: Fire in the barn at about nine at night.
